messages.author: 5ce1f1f0b0b32cf2
messages.subject: lavaan ERROR: mixed + exo in PML not implemented; try optim.gradient = "numerical"
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to run a cross-lagged panel model with three time points and three variables of interest. Two of my variables (FREQ_DEP & CHRONO) are ordinal (4 levels) and one is continuous (OUTDOOR_SUMMER). I have an n of 5,000. 

I am attempting to use this tutorial to fit the model with the pairwise maximum liklihood method: https://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/pml/PL_Tutorial.pdf

Here is my code: 

cl_chrono <- 
'
#Regressions
FREQ_DEP_1~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0 + CHRONO_0
FREQ_DEP_2 ~  FREQ_DEP_1+ OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 + CHRONO_1
CHRONO_1 ~ CHRONO_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0 + FREQ_DEP_0
CHRONO_2 ~  CHRONO_1 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 + FREQ_DEP_1
OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 ~ FREQ_DEP_0 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_0 + CHRONO_0
OUTDOOR_SUMMER_2 ~  FREQ_DEP_1 + OUTDOOR_SUMMER_1 + CHRONO_1
'
fit_cl_chrono <- sem(cl_chrono, data=d, ordered=c("FREQ_DEP_1", "FREQ_DEP_2", "CHRONO_1", "CHRONO_2"), estimator='PML', std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE) 

As you can see above, I declare the relevant endogenous variables as ordered. 

When I run this model, I get the following error and am not sure what it means:  

Error in pml_deriv1(Sigma.hat = Sigma.hat[[g]], Mu.hat = Mu.hat[[g]],  :
  lavaan ERROR: mixed + exo in PML not implemented; try optim.gradient = "numerical"

I have tried following its advice by adding "optim.gradient='numerical'" to my code but so far this model has taken ~20minutes to fit without completing. 

I don't see how my data are any different to the tutorial so am unsure how to proceed and any guidance would be very much appreciated!

Thank you in advance and kind regards,

Angus

can reproduce this?

Yves.

messages.author: 5ce1f1f0b0b32cf2
messages.subject: Re: lavaan ERROR: mixed + exo in PML not implemented; try optim.gradient = "numerical"
parts:
Hi Yves,

Thanks for your response. 
I figured out the issue - the model runs as normal if you specify the pairwise contemporaneous covariances! I.e. correlations between variables within a wave. 

Regards,
Angus
